sources.title: Kazakhstan Embassy in London, Celebration of Kazakhstan’s Independence Day
sources.note: Official account checked for 16 December 1991 independence only; celebratory political evaluations are not adopted.

sources.title: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, address to Parliament, 20 March 2019
sources.note: Official full indexed speech checked: Nazarbayev resignation on 19 March, Tokayev speaking as president on 20 March, and 1995 Constitution. Praise of the first president is not an independent assessment.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, Kazakhstan early presidential election 2022: final report, 14 July 2023
sources.note: Original 37-page PDF directly checked, printed 4 to 5/PDF 6 to 7 political context and constitutional changes; executive summary on competition. Official January casualty numbers are omitted.

sources.title: President of Kazakhstan, official Kazakh text of the Constitution effective 1 July 2026
sources.note: Original official text directly checked, title and Articles 94 to 95; not the superseded 1995 Constitution. Title Romanization is editorial. Group with Constitutional Court explanatory publication as the same constitutional work.

sources.title: Constitutional Court of Kazakhstan, Constitution entered into force on 1 July 2026
sources.note: Original English court announcement checked: referendum 15 March 2026, effective 1 July, previous 1995 Constitution ceased to have legal force. Provides official English title; normative promises are not treated as realized outcomes.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, preliminary assessment of Kazakhstan’s parliamentary election, 24 August 2026
sources.note: Original full page directly checked: 23 August vote, new 145-member Kurultai, party-only nominations, efficient preparations but limited pluralism and counting concerns. Dated preliminary observer findings, not a final report.

sources.title: University of Maryland, Sarah Cameron and The Hungry Steppe, 22 October 2019
sources.note: Original institutional account of historian’s research checked: 1930 to 1933, forced collectivization and livestock confiscation, estimate over 1.5 million deaths, Russian/Kazakh sources. Group Cameron book summaries as one work.

sources.title: CTBTO, International Day Against Nuclear Tests visit to Kazakhstan, 2021
sources.note: Full indexed original account checked; direct fetch 403. More than 450 tests at Semipalatinsk 1949 to 1989; closure 29 August 1991 and renunciation of inherited arsenal. No exaggerated equivalence or precise health-casualty total used.

sources.title: World Bank, Syr Darya Control and Northern Aral Sea project, Water Feature Stories 23, October 2008
sources.note: Original two-page PDF checked: 13 km Kok-Aral Dike completed August 2005; lower salinity and fish harvest recovery by 2007; regional partial restoration, not restoration of entire sea.

sources.title: World Bank, Kazakhstan Monthly Economic Update, February 2026
sources.note: Indexed original update checked: 2025 growth and oil output, domestic consumption sustained by credit despite declining real incomes. No forecast presented as a completed result.

sources.title: NASA, Shuttle-Mir: The United States and Russia Share History’s Highest Stage, Baikonur sidebar
sources.note: Indexed original Baikonur sidebar checked: 1955 construction, Sputnik 1957, Gagarin 1961, lease after Soviet dissolution. Those Soviet achievements are explicitly antecedents, not independent-Kazakhstan inventions.

sources.title: NASA, Three Soyuz crew members launch for two-day trip to station, 2 September 2015
sources.note: Original launch report checked: Aimbetov, Volkov and Mogensen safely in orbit after Baikonur launch. At launch the station had just passed over Kazakhstan. No speculative mission outcomes.

sources.title: UNESCO, Betashar wedding ritual, inscribed 2024
sources.note: Full indexed original entry checked; direct fetch JavaScript challenge. Family welcome, unveiling, song, sweets and coins, learning from elders. Do not universalize to all Kazakhstan households.

sources.title: UNESCO, Orteke performing art, inscribed 2022
sources.note: Full indexed original entry checked; direct fetch challenge. Two-string dombyra, wooden goat puppet, rod/drum, strings to musician’s fingers, skilled performers with three puppets.

sources.title: Akmola regional government, Nauryz kozhe cooking competition
sources.note: Original Russian report directly checked: Kokshetau cultural centre, ten enterprises, seven ingredients in this described recipe, taste and presentation judging, quilt/weaving/felt exhibition. Page lacks a visible date; no invented item year.

sources.title: UNICEF Kazakhstan, Nanosatellites of Hope, 20 June 2022
sources.note: Full original account checked: Amina Pusurmanova aged 17, design/3D printing, assembly, learning KiCad with Uzbek peers, stratospheric launch March 2022. Another UNICEF page differs by one day on launch date, so month only. These were atmospheric flights, not orbit.

sources.title: UNICEF Kazakhstan, A visiting nurse speaks about her profession, 5 June 2023
sources.note: Full original local account checked: Aizharkyn in Zhetysay, home environment, feeding, development, emergency training and referrals. No claim all families receive equal service.

sources.title: WHO, Global Conference on Primary Health Care, Astana, 25 to 26 October 2018
sources.note: Original event account checked: 2018 declaration renews primary-care commitment and commemorates 1978 Alma-Ata. Distinguish international commitment from measured universal care.

sources.title: WHO, Setting standards for WASH in schools: Kazakhstan, 2024
sources.note: Original one-page PDF directly checked. Baseline assessment 153 schools; standard effective January 2024, capacity and disability provisions. Avoid claiming standard already fulfilled everywhere. Campaign name extraction ambiguous, omitted.

proposedOverrides.summary: Independent Kazakhstan through political change, Soviet legacies, spaceflight, family traditions, science education, community healthcare and practical environmental recovery.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Modern Republic only; index 1994 to open, historical independence 16 December 1991. Three geometries cover 1994 to 2000, 2000 to 2010, 2010 to 2020. Astana, Almaty, Semey, Atyrau and Baikonur included; Aktau coastal point excluded, disclosed publicly. Orenburg, Bishkek and Tashkent excluded. No alias to Kazakh Khanate, Soviet Union, Kimek/Kipchak or other steppe identities. New 2026 Constitution verified independently through official Kazakh text, Constitutional Court English statement and ODIHR election observation. No invented fall or successor.
